history_policy: This version hash-inherits every V9 workload, mode, jobs, checksum, timing boundary, engine-availability, acceptance, and runtime-dispatch decision. It versions only the opt-in synchronization and worker-lifecycle attribution inventory; any later workload, boundary, jobs, checksum, metric, or acceptance change creates another version.
change: Adds the existing opt-in per-path synchronization profiler to representative phase snapshots: Thread lock/condition/property waits, queue/channel operations, arena/environment/object lock acquisitions/contentions/spins, worker runs/CPU/max, and thread-join parks/wait. Scored timing rows remain uninstrumented.

tier_attribution.scope: one fresh zig-js process and context per workload and structural variant; synchronization counters are reset before context construction
tier_attribution.invocation: one inherited full-work call with the frozen jobs and lane-zero input
tier_attribution.equivalence: For warmup and invocation independently, each base/variant pair must select the same non-empty set of tree-walker, VM, baseline, optimizer, optimizer-OSR, and deoptimization paths and allocate exactly the same number of environments. Exact tier, runtime, synchronization, and worker counters remain visible rather than normalized away; every Wasm workload must record an invocation-phase Wasm dispatch.
tier_attribution.timing_isolation: Attribution uses fresh opt-in processes and contexts outside every scored timing row; normal contexts retain disabled contention counters and the null execution-attribution pointer.

recognizer_audit.prohibited: Every representative workload identifier is absent from engine source. Identifiers exist only in the owned workload, manifest, and benchmark tooling.
